sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: US Allows Ukrainians and Sudanese to Stay, Temporary Deportation Protections Extended
cards.content: The US Department of Homeland Security has announced that immigrants from Ukraine and Sudan will be allowed to continue living and working in the country without fear of deportation, for now, as their temporary deportation protections were set to expire this week. Over 100,000 Ukrainians and nearly 1,800 Sudanese nationals are currently enrolled in the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) program, which provides humanitarian relief to people fleeing war, natural disasters, or humanitarian crises. Although the Trump administration had previously terminated TPS for multiple countries, including El Salvador earlier this year, the current protections for Ukraine and Sudan will remain in place until further announcements are made. This decision comes after the US Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to end TPS for Haitians and Syrians in June. Meanwhile, immigrants who have lost TPS status in the past have faced uncertainty and fear of detention and deportation.

cards.title: Tiger Shroff survives shooting in Mumbai, two injured in investigation
cards.content: Tiger Shroff, a popular Bollywood actor, was shot at while leaving a football ground in Mumbai, but he survived without sustaining any gunshot wounds. Two people, including his driver, were injured in the attack, which has sent shockwaves through the film industry. The police are investigating and have detained three men in connection with the incident. The attack has raised concerns about Shroff's safety, and celebrities and political figures have spoken out against it. The motive behind the attack is still unclear, but some reports suggest that the Lawrence Bishnoi gang may be involved. The incident has also raised questions about the security of film industry workers and their families.

cards.title: Australian Greens Senator Denies Inappropriate Behavior Allegations
cards.content: Australian Greens Senator Jordon Steele-John has denied allegations of inappropriate behavior towards women, which were brought forward by seven current and former party members. The allegations date back to 2017 and 2025, with the senator claiming they were initially referred to as a nickname, but have since taken on a 'more sinister meaning.' Steele-John also accused party leader David Shoebridge of mishandling the situation and questioned the timing of the letter. An internal party investigation has been launched, and the allegations have been referred to the Independent Parliamentary Standards Commission. In a statement, Steele-John acknowledged the allegations would have damaged the public's trust in him, but expressed his commitment to rebuilding that trust through transparency and accountability.

cards.title: Milky Way ideal for life, study of galaxy simulations shows
cards.content: Researchers have analyzed galaxy simulations to identify the most habitable places in the universe, finding that the Milky Way offers some of the best conditions for life. The team discovered that the Sun's location in the galaxy is ideal, and that the Milky Way's habitable zone is characterized by a balance of factors that make it suitable for life. They also found that other galaxies, particularly smaller and more crowded ones, are less likely to be habitable due to various dangers such as explosions, collisions, and black holes. The study suggests that the Milky Way is typical of the galaxies that have been efficient in creating life-friendly environments, and that it is likely to remain a haven for life in the universe.

cards.title: AI Wearables Raise Privacy Concerns with Continuous Recording
cards.content: The article reports on the growing trend of AI-powered wearables and devices that record, transcribe, and analyze a user's daily life. Chris Thomas, a Pittsburgh-based business owner, uses a range of AI gadgets, including Meta's camera-equipped glasses and Amazon's Bee wearable, to stay organized and pay bills on time. However, these devices have raised concerns about privacy, with some users worrying about being recorded without their consent. The article highlights the legal questions surrounding the use of AI devices, including whether continuous listening and interpreting of speech can be considered an interception. The development of AI devices that can rapidly interpret and draw meaning from large volumes of information has raised concerns about the erosion of privacy, with experts warning that people can be swept into AI-powered surveillance without owning or knowingly interacting with the device doing the collecting.

cards.title: Honeybee colony can be considered as a single living Organism
cards.content: A new study proposes that a honey bee colony functions as a superorganism, meaning a group of individual bees that work together like the specialized cells of a single living organism. Researchers suggest that the colony has its own life cycle, including development, reproduction through swarming (when a queen leaves with part of the colony to establish a new hive), aging, and eventual death. This perspective challenges conventional beekeeping practices such as frequently replacing queens and preventing swarming, as these interventions may disrupt the colony’s natural reproductive cycle and ability to manage parasites such as Varroa mites. However, further research is needed to determine whether managing colonies according to this superorganism model can improve bee health and parasite control

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Type 2 Diabetes Patients With Stable Rhythms Control Blood Sugar Better
cards.content: Patients with type 2 diabetes who use insulin have a better chance of controlling their blood sugar levels if they have a consistent daily rhythm. Researchers found that patients with the most stable daily rhythms were 2.3 times more likely to meet their blood sugar goals compared to those with less stable rhythms. The study, which involved 122 patients, also found that patients who were more active in the afternoon had smaller swings in their blood sugar levels. Additionally, patients who got sufficient sleep had a lower risk of having low blood sugar and smaller glucose fluctuations. The researchers believe that maintaining regular daily rhythms can help manage blood sugar levels and plan to conduct a follow-up study to confirm this.

cards.title: Scientists Study 'Immortal Jellyfish' Rejuvenation Secrets
cards.content: Scientists have discovered a unique property of the Turritopsis dohrnii jellyfish, also known as the 'immortal jellyfish', which can rewind its life cycle and revert to a younger state. This process involves a transformation of adult cells into stem cells, allowing the jellyfish to create a new polyp and eventually grow into adult jellyfish again. Researchers are studying the genetic and molecular processes behind this phenomenon, hoping to unlock its secrets and potentially apply them to human cells to treat age-related diseases. While the goal is not to reverse human aging entirely, scientists aim to explore ways to coax human cells into more youthful states to heal wounds and treat age-related maladies. The research is still in its early stages, but initial findings suggest that the immortal jellyfish's ability to rejuvenate may be linked to its enhanced ability to repair DNA damage and maintain telomeres, which could hold the key to understanding and potentially applying its regenerative abilities to humans.

cards.title: Avalanche Sweeps Away Over 100 Sheep in Himachal Pradesh
cards.content: In October 2025, Joginder Chand, a 50-year-old shepherd from Himachal Pradesh's Chamba district, set out to migrate his 600 sheep and goats to warmer grazing grounds in Kangra district. Suddenly, an avalanche swept away over 100 animals.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

sections.title: Entertainment

cards.title: Sunderland Music City gets £156,166 grant for heritage project
cards.content: A major heritage project, Sunderland Music City's Mackem Music Memories, has been awarded £156,166 by the National Lottery Heritage Fund to preserve the city's musical history. The project aims to collect over 300 memories of Sunderland's music scene from residents past and present through questionnaires, research, and interviews. The memories will be displayed in an exhibition at the Culture House Sunderland in summer 2027, along with community activities and live events. The project will also work with diverse communities, including South Asian, Filipino, Nigerian, and Eastern European groups, and international students. The goal is to capture these stories before they disappear and make them part of Sunderland's permanent heritage.

cards.title: Paul Shipper: From Film Fan to Illustrator of Marvel and Star Wars
cards.content: Paul Shipper, a film fan-turned-illustrator, has come a long way from creating movie poster artwork for fun. He has worked on some of Hollywood's biggest franchises, including Marvel, Indiana Jones, and Star Wars. Shipper's passion for illustration started when he was a kid, inspired by the films of George Lucas and Steven Spielberg. He shared his designs online, which led to opportunities that once seemed like a dream. The illustrator has worked on various projects, including posters and artwork for blockbuster titles, and has maintained a consistent artistic style despite working across different projects. Shipper is now involved in a charity exhibition, AMPjam Presents: We've Been Framed, which brings together more than 60 artists from around the world to create original artworks inspired by films and television shows.

cards.title: Scottish Actor Hopes Fans Accept His Accent in Marvel Series
cards.content: Scottish actor Ruaridh Mollica, who plays Tommy Maximoff in the Marvel Cinematic Universe miniseries VisionQuest, hopes fans will accept his Scottish accent. He says speaking in his own accent helped him bring the character to life, and he's excited to be part of the show.

cards.title: Criminals use AI to create fake UK retailers, warns National Trading Standards
cards.content: Beware of online scams, warns National Trading Standards, as criminals are using artificial intelligence (AI) to create fake websites and convincing fake products. These scams often claim to be family-owned UK retailers selling quality products, but the reality is that products either don't arrive or are cheap imports from countries like China. AI-generated images, voice cloning, and deepfake videos are all being used to trick people out of their money. Old tactics like spotting typos and grammatical errors are no longer reliable, as AI can now mimic legitimate-looking websites. To protect yourself, stop and think before paying or sharing personal information, and be wary of pressure or urgency. You can report fraud and scams to Report Fraud or by calling the Citizens Advice Consumer Helpline.

cards.title: ChangXin Predicts Profitability in 2026, Driven by AI Demand Growth
cards.content: a Chinese chipmaker, ChangXin Memory Technologies, expects to reverse a net loss and become profitable in the first nine months of 2026, with a predicted net profit of 131-132.5 billion yuan. The company's revenue is also expected to increase by 232.9-237.9 billion yuan, driven by growing demand for AI computing power. This growth has led to supply shortages and higher prices in the global DRAM market. ChangXin has been gaining ground in the global memory chip market, now accounting for 10% of global DRAM revenue, up from 5% a year earlier.
